## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One fix is needed before this lands. `refresh_fingerprints` overwrites the stored digest for every name it is given, including files already in the manifest. If a tracked file has been hand-edited and is passed alongside new files, it is quietly re-baselined, and `verify` can no longer detect the edit, although the PR description says detecting such edits is the point of existing fingerprints. `register_new_files` is not affected: it keeps existing entries, and its test shows that.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/integrity.py:17 — correctness — If `tracked.txt` has been hand-edited since it was fingerprinted, calling `refresh_fingerprints(root, manifest, ["tracked.txt", "new.txt"])` replaces its stored digest with the digest of the edited content, so `verify` afterwards returns `True` instead of `False`. Line 17 assigns `entries[name] = fingerprint(root / name)` with no `name not in entries` check. The PR body says existing fingerprints let verification "detect hand-edited tracked files", and the added test at tests/test_integrity.py:44 calls refresh with this mixed tracked-plus-new list, but only on an unedited tracked file. That test would pass with or without the overwrite, so it cannot catch this. Recommended fix: skip names already present in `entries`, or raise when an existing entry's digest differs, like `register_new_files` does. Then add a test that edits `tracked.txt` before refreshing and asserts `not verify(...)`. — An operator who runs the refresh after adding files can unknowingly approve a tampered tracked file, and integrity verification then misses exactly the case it exists to catch.

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- `test_register_preserves_existing_fingerprints` (tests/test_integrity.py:53-66) edits a tracked file before registering. It checks that the old digest is kept, that `verify` then fails, and it covers duplicate names and an empty list.
